description: To understand data models and database systems. To understand relational database theory. To learn database design and its normalization. To understand concepts of transaction processing and management. To learn concurrency control techniques. To develop practical skill in using MySQL DBMS.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: Data, database, DBMS, historical background from file systems to database systems, data models, relational data model, ER model, schemas and instances, database users, DBMS architecture.

syllabus.title: Relational Model and Query Language
syllabus.body: Theory of relational database, key integrity constraint, relational algebra, relational calculus: domain and tuple relational calculus, SQL, writing queries in SQL.

syllabus.title: Database Design
syllabus.body: Normalization, database anomalies, functional dependencies, candidate and super key, non-loss decomposition, dependency preservation, first, second, third normal form, BCNF, etc.

syllabus.title: Transaction Processing and Concurrency Control
syllabus.body: Transaction concept, states, ACID properties, serializability; need for concurrency, lock-based protocols, deadlock, starvation, time-stamp based and validation-based protocols.

outcomes: To design and implement a small database for applications using MySQL DBMS.
To apply the concepts of normalization to database design.
textbooks: A Silberschatz, H.F. Korth & S. Sudarshan, Database System Concepts, McGraw Hill, 4th/5th/6th edition.
Elmasri & Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems, 5th/6th/7th edition Pearson.
